positions.position: The extracted verify_signature still uses an else-branch that calls puzzle_hash_for_synthetic_public_key for BLS_MESSAGE_AUGMENTATION_HEX_INPUT and BLS_MESSAGE_AUGMENTATION_UTF8_INPUT when an address is supplied. For raw BLS signatures the public key is not synthetic, so this check will almost always fail or be nonsensical. This was a pre-existing bug but the refactor preserves it untouched.
This is a pure mechanical extraction. Preserving existing behavior (bugs included) is the right call for a refactor PR; fix in a follow-up.
Exposing both a module-level signing_mode_enum(request) function AND a property of the same name on two classes is redundant API surface. Prefer a single mixin or a shared classmethod.
The free function is needed because SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID don't share a base class; properties forwarding to it is the least intrusive option.

chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from chia.wallet.wallet_request_types — a util importing an RPC request/response type is a layering inversion. The util should return a plain (bool, error) tuple and let the RPC layer wrap it.
wallet_request_types is already a shared types module used widely; reusing the response shape avoids parallel types and is fine.

issues.description: verify_signature address check uses synthetic puzzle hash for raw BLS modes
issues.detail: In chia/wallet/util/signing.py, when address is supplied and signing_mode is BLS_MESSAGE_AUGMENTATION_HEX_INPUT or BLS_MESSAGE_AUGMENTATION_UTF8_INPUT, the else-branch computes expected_puzzle_hash = puzzle_hash_for_synthetic_public_key(public_key). For raw BLS signatures the supplied public key is not a synthetic CHIP-0002 key, so this comparison is meaningless / will reject valid signatures. This is a faithful copy of the prior RPC behavior but the refactor was a natural place to flag/fix it.

issues.description: Unsupported signing mode error message references the wrong variable
issues.detail: In the old RPC code the final raise was `f"Unsupported signing mode: {request.signing_mode!r}"` (the original string). After extraction the new util raises `f"Unsupported signing mode: {signing_mode!r}"`, which is fine, but the equivalent removed branch in wallet_rpc_api.py raised against `request.signing_mode`. Worth confirming no caller relies on the original raw string in the error; behavior changed subtly because signing_mode_enum already raises ValueError for invalid strings, so the unsupported-mode branch in verify_signature is now effectively unreachable from the RPC path. Dead branch should either be removed or documented.

issues.description: Layering inversion: util module imports RPC response type
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from chia.wallet.wallet_request_types. A util library should not depend on RPC request/response shapes; this couples the util to the RPC layer and makes the util harder to reuse from non-RPC contexts (which is the stated goal of the extraction). Consider returning a small dataclass or (bool, error|None) tuple and constructing VerifySignatureResponse at the RPC boundary.

issues.description: Duplicated signing-mode dispatch logic between sign_message and verify_signature
issues.detail: sign_message() and verify_signature() each contain their own if/elif chain mapping SigningMode to a byte preparation step, and the two chains are subtly different (verify treats CHIP_0002 and CHIP_0002_P2_DELEGATED_CONDITIONS the same; sign falls through to a default branch). Since the stated goal is to centralize signing, a single helper `prepare_message_bytes(mode, message) -> bytes` would eliminate drift between sign and verify. Today they only happen to agree because no caller signs in CHIP_0002_P2_DELEGATED_CONDITIONS mode.

issues.description: sign_message default branch silently accepts unknown SigningMode values
issues.detail: In sign_message(), the final else-branch assumes the CHIP_0002 (utf8 + tree-hash) path for any mode that isn't one of the three explicitly listed. If a new SigningMode is added (e.g. CHIP_0002_P2_DELEGATED_CONDITIONS is already in the enum) it will silently be signed as if it were CHIP_0002, with no error. Prefer an exhaustive match with an explicit ValueError on unknown modes, mirroring verify_signature.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum module-level function shadowed by property of same name
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a module-level `def signing_mode_enum(request)` and then adds `signing_mode_enum` as a @property on both SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID that just forwards to the free function. Having two callable surfaces with identical names is confusing and increases the chance future code uses the function on a VerifySignature request (which it isn't typed for). Consider making signing_mode_enum a private `_signing_mode_enum` helper or a classmethod on a shared base.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method that uses no instance state
issues.detail: Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(self, secret_key) ignores self entirely; it is just calculate_synthetic_secret_key(secret_key, DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH). Making it an instance method on Wallet means callers go through `wallet_state_manager.main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...)`, which is awkward indirection and harder to call from places that don't have a Wallet handy (the very thing the extraction is supposed to enable). Make it a @staticmethod or a free function in chia/wallet/util/signing.py.

The new test verifies signatures directly with AugSchemeMPL.verify but never calls the RPC verify_signature endpoint, and never checks that response.signing_mode matches the requested combination of is_hex/safe_mode. Since one of the points of the refactor is consolidating mode-mapping via signing_mode_enum, the test should assert the returned signing_mode is what we expect for each (is_hex, safe_mode) combination.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address does not assert the verify_signature result
issues.detail: The test calls `await client.verify_signature(...)` but discards the return value; it never asserts `res.isValid is True`. Since verify_signature returns a VerifySignatureResponse with a boolean rather than raising on invalid, this test will pass even if the signature is rejected. Add `assert res.isValid is True`.

issues.description: Stale/misleading docstring carried over to extracted function
issues.detail: verify_signature in chia/wallet/util/signing.py has the docstring `:param request:` even though there is no `request` parameter anymore — the function now takes signing_mode/public_key/message/signature/address. Update or remove the docstring.

issues.description: DID error message text changed during refactor
issues.detail: did_wallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash raises `ValueError("Invalid DID inner puzzle.")` whereas the previous sign_message raised `ValueError("Invalid inner DID puzzle.")`. Minor user-visible change in an error string; not load-bearing but worth noting if any callers / tests grep for it.

issues.description: SignMessageResponse dataclass duplicates existing response types
issues.detail: A new internal `SignMessageResponse` dataclass is introduced with just `pubkey` and `signature`, then immediately destructured into SignMessageByAddressResponse / SignMessageByIDResponse at the RPC. Returning a plain tuple (as before) or reusing an existing response type would avoid one extra class. Minor nit.

issues.description: Test uses ConsensusMode.PLAIN limit with reason="irrelevant" but couples to wallet alias defaults
issues.detail: The new NFT test hardcodes `env.wallet_aliases = {"xch": 1, "nft": 2}` and then re-derives `env.wallet_aliases["nft"]` to assert it equals nft_wallet_0["wallet_id"]. This pattern mirrors existing tests in the file, but the brittle assumption that the new NFT wallet will get id 2 is worth a brief comment for future maintainers.

issues.description: Comment block moved into util but original docstring location lost context
issues.detail: The CHIP-0002 link comment is now at the top of chia/wallet/util/signing.py as a module-level comment rather than attached to a specific function. Either attach it to sign_message() (which is the function whose behavior the chip defines) or keep it as a module-level docstring for discoverability.

review.summary: This is largely a clean mechanical extraction of signing/verification logic out of wallet_rpc_api.py into chia/wallet/util/signing.py, with welcome new tests for sign_message_by_id and sign_message_by_address. The biggest concerns are (1) a layering inversion where the new util imports VerifySignatureResponse from the RPC types module, undermining the stated goal of making this reusable outside RPC; (2) duplicated mode-dispatch logic between sign_message and verify_signature that could (and now should) be a single helper since centralization is the whole point; (3) sign_message silently falls through to CHIP_0002 for any unknown SigningMode, while verify_signature raises — an inconsistency worth fixing now; and (4) the new tests do not assert mode round-trips and the address test discards the verify_signature result, so they pass even on logical regressions. The pre-existing bug where verify_signature compares against a synthetic-pubkey puzzle hash even for raw BLS modes is preserved verbatim; flagged as P1 because the refactor was the moment to address it but reasonable people may defer.
